A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NNiT work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite appendix reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ManiSkill3 policy-generation experiments, GHN-versus-SGD comparisons, weight-diversity analyses, and simulated policy rollouts.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds permutation, representational-similarity, performance-distribution, MNIST classification, and joint-sampling analyses.

M1.justification: The GHN/CNN weight generator, patch tokenization, architecture tokens, transformer backbone, MoNL objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged. MNIST applies the existing pipeline to another task; the permutation experiment ablates its training data.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates robotic control on three ManiSkill3 tasks. v2 retains these and adds MNIST classification with inputs reduced to 32 dimensions by PCA, substantially extending empirical coverage into supervised image classification (Appendix H).

E2.justification: Table 2 retains SANE and D2NWG for both seen and unseen architectures, and the alignment comparison retains GHN and SGD. Added analyses reuse existing comparison methods; the permutation condition is an ablation of NNiT.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation with CKA measurements, function-preserving permutation controls, 80-policy mean and worst-architecture summaries, and MNIST accuracy evaluation using PCA fitted on the training split. The original 64/8 architecture split, 50-episode evaluation, and top-10-from-100 protocol remain stated. The relationship between the new 80-policy analysis and that 100-sample protocol is unexplained.

E4.justification: New Appendix C tests representational diversity and whether destroying alignment prevents successful generation. Appendix F examines selection effects through unselected and worst-architecture performance, while Appendix I quantifies architecture diversity under unconditional sampling. These substantially extend v1's heatmaps, parameter-distance analyses, and illustrative rollouts.

E5.justification: The existing seed counts and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged. New CKA entries use the already present mean-plus/minus format without introducing a defined uncertainty estimator, confidence interval, significance test, or additional replication protocol. Generated-policy counts concern evaluation sampling rather than repeated training runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their results. New Table 9 reports NNiT mean success of 78.8%, 74.7%, and 54.9% versus D2NWG's 15.6%, 60.0%, and 12.2% on PickCube, PushCube, and StackCubeEasy. Additional findings include the permutation ablation's 78.8%-to-0% contrast, CKA scores, 96.1% mean MNIST accuracy, and 53 unique architectures among 100 joint samples. These are added results, not improvements to the retained scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–5 are substantively unchanged. The MoNL derivation moves from Appendix C to Appendix A. New empirical analyses introduce no theorem, proof, or revised formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add the claim that the same pipeline generalizes to MNIST classification beyond robotics. The three principal contributions and the existing architecture-generation and robotic-control claims remain intact.

C2.justification: New discussion argues that the performance advantage persists beyond top-10 selection and connects task tolerances to weight-generation precision. Appendix C interprets permutation failure as dependence on spatial ordering; Appendix H acknowledges the current input-scale constraint requiring PCA. These refine the existing account without replacing it, and Section 7's limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents MNIST's training-split PCA reduction from 784 to 32 dimensions and network filtering, and newly specifies robotics success tolerances. Existing dataset-generation and diffusion hyperparameters are retained in relocated Tables 7 and 8; the PDFs do not establish changes to those settings.

R1.justification: The reference lists contain the same works, and the substantive positioning relative to weight-generation methods, GHNs, and diffusion transformers is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and heading edits, adds acknowledgements and appendix cross-references, and reorganizes existing supplementary sections. MoNL moves earlier, dataset generation moves later, and implementation details become a separate appendix. The main narrative is largely preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds the CKA and full-distribution tables, relocates existing appendix displays, and swaps the numbering of the anchoring heatmaps and diversity histograms. The histogram display is more compact, while existing diagrams, heatmaps, rollouts, and main result-table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 supported alignment mainly through visualizations and parameter diversity, and emphasized selected top-10 performance. v2 adds a controlled permutation ablation, representational-diversity evidence, and unselected and worst-architecture results (Appendices C and F), substantially strengthening support for the central mechanism and making performance reporting more informative. MNIST provides additional cross-domain evidence. The unexplained 80-versus-100 sampling relationship and absence of MNIST comparators limit completeness, but do not outweigh these substantial evidentiary gains.
